translations.translatedText: # Saturday 29.12.2018 (radio)

Free opening hours did not bring more jobs to shops. Finns look forward to next year with a positive mood. The citizens' initiative on fireworks is moving on to Parliament. Christmas book sales started slowly this year.
## Free opening hours benefit big shops
![Apples in the fruit section of a shop.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10278036)
Open image viewer
Photo: Elisa Kinnunen / Yle
Free opening hours in shops have increased the sales of big shops. Big supermarkets have been the biggest winners of the liberalisation. Smaller shops have suffered the most.
Free opening hours have not brought more jobs. Statistics Finland says that working hours have been somewhat lower than in 2015.
The restrictions were removed in January 2016. Representatives of the retail trade justified the liberalisation of opening hours by saying that more jobs would have to come.
## Finns look to the new year with a positive mood
![Graphic](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10574351)
Open image viewer
Photo: Yle News Graphics
Finns look forward to next year with a positive mood.
37 percent of Finns believe that the year 2019 will be personally better for them than this year has been. Only 14 percent believe that their own life will go in a worse direction next year.
Instead, 65 percent of Finns believe that next year will be a more restless year in the world than this year.
The information comes from a survey by Taloustutkimus. It is part of an international study that included 50 countries in total.
## The citizens' initiative on fireworks goes to Parliament
![A man fires fireworks. ](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-8566059)
Open image viewer
Fireworks can cause serious eye injuries. A rocket must never be launched without protective glasses. Photo: Sari Gustafsson / Lehtikuva
The citizens' initiative on the use of fireworks is moving on to Parliament.
The citizens' initiative wants to ban ordinary people from setting off fireworks. Fireworks are to be only for professionals to use.
The citizens' initiative gathered 50,000 names, and Parliament will begin to handle the initiative.

Several organisations stand behind the citizens' initiative, such as animal organisations and disability organisations. They want to reduce, for example, eye injuries caused by fireworks. So far this millennium more than 500 eye injuries caused by fireworks have been registered in Finland.
The initiative does not want to ban sparklers, small bangers and fountains.
The law allows fireworks to be used only from the evening of New Year's Eve, at 6 pm, until 2 am in the early morning.
## Christmas book sales started late
![Women browse a book by Michelle Obama in the Finnish Bookshop](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10574312)
Open image viewer
Photo: Mesut Turan / Lehtikuva
Christmas book sales started slowly this year. Many books were sold only in the days just after Christmas.
Bookshop owners say that one reason is, for example, that tax refunds were paid late this year. In addition, Christmas Eve fell on a Monday.
Preliminary statistics show that sales did not rise from last year.
Christmas sales are important for bookshops and publishers, because up to 40 percent of the year's book sales come in the last part of the year.
This Christmas's favourite books were Kari Hotakainen's book about formula star Kimi Räikkönen and Michelle Obama's biography.
